items.q: In the diagnosis block, which kidney morphology is listed for a CKD work-up?
All but one are in the 'all of' set written for diabetic nephropathy. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Diabetic nephropathy — all of: proteinuria, edema, hypertension, retinopathy. (Book p806)

items.q: Fill up: The diagnosis block closes with a biopsy line looking for IF, TA and ______.
The five numbered reversible causes to address include obstruction and ______.
items.exp: Address reversible causes: 1. obstruction; 2. drugs/toxins/alternate medicines; 3. uncontrolled hypertension; 4. ECF volume ↓; 5. hypercalcemia. (Book p806)

items.q: Uncontrolled hypertension is numbered which item in the reversible-causes list?
items.exp: Numbered list: 1 obstruction, 2 drugs/toxins/alternate medicines, 3 uncontrolled hypertension, 4 ECF volume ↓, 5 hypercalcemia. (Book p806)

items.q: Match the following reversible cause to its detail — 1) ECF volume ↓  2) Hypercalcemia  3) Drugs … A) Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus + afferent arteriole vasoconstriction  B) Diuretic excess / ↓ albumin  C) Toxins and alternate medicines
items.exp: Reversible causes: ECF volume ↓ d/t diuretic excess, ↓ albumin; hypercalcemia → nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, afferent arteriole vasoconstriction; drugs/toxins/alternate medicines. (Book p806)

items.q: A CKD patient on aggressive diuretics with hypoalbuminemia develops worsening renal function. The reversible mechanism named in the list is:
opts: ECF volume ↓ from diuretic excess and ↓ albumin
items.exp: Reversible cause 4: ECF volume ↓ d/t diuretic excess / ↓ albumin. (Book p806)

items.q: Hypercalcemia is listed as a reversible cause because it drives nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and afferent arteriole vasoconstriction.
opts: True, but only in dialysis patients
items.exp: Reversible cause 5: hypercalcemia → nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, afferent arteriole vasoconstriction. (Book p806)
